title: Nearly half of buy now, pay later users say they've had problems like overspending
summary: News wire article cites a Bankrate survey finding nearly half of BNPL users report problems like overspending or missed payments.

assertions.quote: close to half have reported problems including overspending, missing payments and regretting their purchases

verdicts.note: Directly measured by Bankrate's survey of BNPL users, which found 49% reported at least one related problem.

CFPB cites US consumer surveys finding 'between 20 and 50 percent of BNPL consumers regret their purchases,' but cautions that 'the surveys' differing methodologies and the ambiguity of what counts as "BNPL" in each limit how much weight any single figure can bear.'

assertions.quote: the best way to use buy now, pay later is to isolate a single large purchase, hopefully something necessary
buyers can quickly overspend if they're stacking purchases of $20 here and $50 there without adequately keeping track
Gen Zers were the most likely to have encountered issues. Two-thirds of those users ages 18-28 told Bankrate they've experienced at least one problem
some installment plans are lasting longer and charging interest now

verdicts.note: Matches Bankrate's reporting that providers are extending loan terms and adding interest charges beyond the original interest-free pay-in-4 model.
KC Fed endnote: many BNPL providers also offer longer-term loans charging interest up to nearly 30% APR, making that segment of the industry behave more like credit cards.
